cues.zh: 为什么这些60美元的游戏都想卖我开箱？
cues.en: Why are all of these $60 games trying to sell me loot boxes?

cues.zh: 为什么这些60美元的游戏都在卖季票和DLC？
cues.en: Why are all these $60 games selling me season passes for their DLC?

cues.zh: 为什么这些60美元的游戏都包含内购？
cues.en: Why are all of these $60 games including microtransactions?

cues.zh: 为什么这些60美元的游戏第一天就想卖我DLC？
cues.en: Why are all of these $60 games trying to sell me DLC on day one?

cues.zh: 说法五花八门，但问的核心问题都一样：
cues.en: There are many variations, but the fundamental question being asked is the same:

cues.zh: 为什么它们想让我为这游戏付超过60美元？
cues.en: Why are they trying to make me pay more than $60 for this game?

cues.zh: 今天，我们就来回答这个问题。
cues.en: Today, we are going to answer that question.

cues.zh: AAA游戏不该再卖60美元了。
cues.en: AAA games should not cost $60 anymore.

cues.zh: 接下来我会用整期视频解释原因。
cues.en: And I'm going to spend the rest of this video explaining why.

cues.zh: AAA游戏定在60美元，大约是高清主机发售的时候：
cues.en: The price for a AAA game was set at $60 right around the launch of HD consoles:

cues.zh: Xbox 360和PS3。
cues.en: The Xbox 360 and the PS3.

cues.zh: 那是2005年前后，之后价格就再没变过。
cues.en: That was around 2005 and the price hasn't shifted again since.

cues.zh: 但美元的购买力确实变了。
cues.en: But the value of the U.S. Dollar certainly has.

cues.zh: 过去十年的平均通胀率大约是每年 2%。
cues.en: The rate of inflation over the last decade has averaged out to roughly 2% per year.

cues.zh: 根据我能找到的最佳数据，这意味着从我们开始以 60 美元卖游戏以来，商品价格已经上涨了 25.34%。
cues.en: According to the best figures I can find, that means that the value of goods has inflated 25.34% since we started selling games for $60.

cues.zh: 为了简化计算，我们就把它向下取整到 25%。
cues.en: And let's just round that down to a flat 25% to keep the math simple.

cues.zh: 所以光是考虑通胀，AAA 游戏现在就该卖 75 美元。
cues.en: So due to inflation alone, AAA games should be selling for $75 right now.

cues.zh: 但显然，通胀并不是唯一的影响因素。
cues.en: But obviously, inflation isn't the only factor in play here.

cues.zh: 所有 AAA 游戏都在争着做出市面上画面最好的游戏。
cues.en: AAA games are all competing to have the best looking game on the market.

cues.zh: 而这场画面竞赛每到新一代主机推出时，成本都会大幅增加。
cues.en: And that graphical arms race gets way more expensive with each new console generation.

cues.zh: 当然，这一路上我们也找到不少巧妙的方法来提高效率、降低成本。
cues.en: And, sure, we have found a lot of clever efficiencies along the way to reduce costs.

cues.zh: 我是说，天哪，我们现在把第三方游戏引擎当作中间件来用，这省了一大笔钱。
cues.en: I mean, heck, we treat third-party game engines like middleware now, and that saves tons.

cues.zh: 但即便有这些节省，我估计3A游戏的制作成本大约是2005年的三到四倍。
cues.en: But even with those savings, I would estimate that AAA games cost somewhere between three and four times as much to make as they did back in 2005.

cues.zh: 那么……这是不是意味着游戏现在应该卖225到300美元？
cues.en: So... does that mean games should actually be costing somewhere between $225 and $300?

cues.zh: 幸运的是，并不是。情况没那么糟。
cues.en: Fortunately, no. Things aren't quite that dire.

cues.zh: 这个很难有精确数字，但现在的游戏玩家群体也比2005年大得多。
cues.en: It's pretty hard to pin down exact numbers on this, but the game playing audience is a lot bigger than it was in 2005, too.

cues.zh: 大概大了好几倍。
cues.en: Like, several times bigger.

cues.zh: 这意味着有更多的客户可以销售，这有助于弥补更高的制作成本。
cues.en: And that means that there's a lot more customers to sell to, which helps to make up for that higher production cost.

cues.zh: 而且如果你成功做出爆款，还能带来更大的利润。
cues.en: And can result In even bigger profits, IF you manage to make a huge hit.

cues.zh: Unfortunately，当你指望更高的销量来盈利时，如果游戏扑街了……
cues.en: Unfortunately, when you're counting on that higher number of sales to make a profit, if your game flops...

cues.zh: 嗯，你会亏掉一笔大到离谱、甚至可能拖垮整个工作室的钱。
cues.en: Well, you're gonna be losing an impossibly large, possibly studio-sinking amount of money.

cues.zh: 但既然我们只关注游戏的平均零售价应该是多少，那就先忽略这个增加的风险因素吧。
cues.en: But, since we're just focusing on what the average retail price of a game should be, let's just ignore that increased risk factor for now.

cues.zh: 基于我们在这个行业里亲身看到的情况……
cues.en: Based on what we've seen firsthand working in this industry...

cues.zh: （不幸的是，其中大部分都受保密协议约束）
cues.en: (much of which is under NDA, unfortunately)

cues.zh: ……如果我非得凭直觉估个数——请理解，这真的只是个粗略猜测……
cues.en: ...if I had to make a gut estimate - and understand this really is just a rough guess...

cues.zh: 我会说，一款现代3A游戏的实际零售价，在没有任何额外持续收入来源支撑的情况下……
cues.en: I would say that the actual retail price of a modern AAA game, without any additional ongoing revenue sources to support it...

cues.zh: ……全新售价大概应该高达85到90美元。
cues.en: ...should probably be as high as $85 to $90 new.

cues.zh: 可以理解，这个数字让整个行业感到恐慌。
cues.en: Now, understandably, that number freaks the industry out.

cues.zh: 澳大利亚以外，谁会花 90 美元买一款电子游戏？
cues.en: Who outside of Australia is gonna pay $90 for a video game?

cues.zh: 我是说，我们都看到了 Neo Geo 的下场。
cues.en: I mean, we all saw what happened to the Neo Geo.

cues.zh: 而这种恐惧，又因为移动游戏市场的成功而加剧了……
cues.en: And this fear has been compounded by the success of the mobile game market...

cues.zh: ……这在一定程度上训练了消费者，让他们觉得游戏就该便宜得惊人。
cues.en: ...which has sort of trained consumers to think that games should be astonishingly cheap.

cues.zh: 我是说，对一款平板游戏来说，10 美元就算贵了。
cues.en: I mean, for a tablet game, $10 is considered expensive.

cues.zh: 哪怕同一款游戏在 DS 上要 30 美元，在 Steam 上要 40 美元。
cues.en: Even if that same game would cost $30 on the DS or $40 on Steam.

cues.zh: 说到这个，Steam 促销也一直在训练我们期待更便宜的游戏。
cues.en: For that matter, Steam Sales have been training us to expect cheaper games, too.

cues.zh: 于是行业就把 60 美元这个价格一直维持在原位。
cues.en: And so the industry has kept that $60 price right where it is.

cues.zh: 而且，我是说，也许他们这么做是对的。
cues.en: And, I mean, maybe they're right to do so.

cues.zh: 2005 年价格涨到 60 美元时，很多人可是相当不满。
cues.en: A lot of people got pretty bent out of shape when the price got bumped up to $60 back in 2005.

cues.zh: 而70这个数字总让人感觉像是……
cues.en: And there is something about the number 70 that just feels like...

cues.zh: [猛吸一口气]哎呀，这可是一大笔钱。
cues.en: [breathes in sharply] Yikes, that's a lot of money.

cues.zh: 行业智慧在这里可能真的说对了。
cues.en: Industry wisdom really may be right here.

cues.zh: 也许把标准价格提高到60美元以上确实会导致销量下降。
cues.en: Maybe raising that standard price any higher than $60 WOULD lead to a drop in sales.

cues.zh: 但是！不涨价的话，我们就把自己逼到了困境中。
cues.en: But! By not raising prices, we've sort of put ourselves in a tough spot.

cues.zh: 如果我们要覆盖开发成本、降低灾难性损失的风险……
cues.en: If we are gonna cover our development costs, reduce the risk of catastrophic losses...

cues.zh: ……并向股东展示他们期望的回报率，我们就必须想办法增加收入。
cues.en: ...and show our shareholders the return percentages they're expecting, we've gotta do something to increase revenue.

cues.zh: 我们尝试了很多不同的方法，成效参差不齐。
cues.en: And we've tried to do that in a lot of different ways, to varying degrees of success.

cues.zh: 首先，我们尝试通过销售DLC来增加收入。
cues.en: First, we tried increasing revenue by selling DLC.

cues.zh: 但如果在游戏发售时就卖DLC，粉丝会不满；如果晚些再发布DLC，他们又不买。
cues.en: But fans got upset if we sold that DLC at launch, and they didn't buy it if we released the DLC later.

cues.zh: 接下来，我们尝试将游戏设计成永久体验。
cues.en: Next, we tried designing games to be perpetual experiences.

cues.zh: 那种你可以玩上一整年的游戏，
cues.en: Games that you would play all year long,

cues.zh: 因为这样一来，我们就能在游戏更长的生命周期里售卖地图包和扩展内容。
cues.en: Because then, we could sell map packs and expansions over that game's longer lifespan.

cues.zh: 但长期支持这些游戏成本也相当高昂，而且并非适用于所有类型的游戏。
cues.en: But supporting those games long-term turned out to be pretty expensive too, and it didn't really work for every kind of game.

cues.zh: 此外，玩家同时能积极跟进的永久游戏数量有限。
cues.en: Besides, players can only actively keep up with so many perpetual games at once.

cues.zh: 所以，所有这些永久游戏都得争夺注意力，而受众就被锁定了。
cues.en: So, all of those perpetual games have to compete for attention and the audience just gets locked down.

cues.zh: 就像当年MMORPG泛滥一样。
cues.en: It's like the MMORPG flood all over again.

cues.zh: 于是，现在我们又在尝试下一个点子：开箱。
cues.en: And so, now we are trying the next thing: loot boxes.

cues.zh: 几周后我们会专门讨论开箱这个话题，但基本上这就是我们目前的处境。
cues.en: We'll come back to the specific topic of loot boxes in a couple of weeks, but this is basically where we're at.

cues.zh: 而现在，作为受众的我们必须决定自己想要什么。
cues.en: And now, we as an audience have to decide what we want.

cues.zh: 我们能接受在零售时花更多钱买这些游戏吗？
cues.en: Are we okay with paying more for these games at retail?

cues.zh: 70美元？
80美元？
甚至可能更多？
cues.en: Maybe even more?

cues.zh: 数据表明答案是否定的，但如果是这样的话……
cues.en: The data suggests that the answer is no, but if that's the case...

cues.zh: 那我们就得学会接受开箱、微交易，或者行业接下来尝试的其他模式。
cues.en: Well, we're gonna have to learn to live with loot boxes or microtransactions or whatever other model the industry attempts next.

cues.zh: 我说的“学会接受”，不是指忍受那些掠夺性的破玩意儿。
cues.en: And by learn to live with, I don't mean put up with predatory crap.

cues.zh: 我是说，我们得找到一种方式，奖励开发者做出好的补充收入系统……
cues.en: I mean, we're gonna have to find a way to reward developers for making good supplementary income systems...

cues.zh: ……这些系统不过度激进，也完全不要求你为了竞技而付费。
cues.en: ...that aren't overly aggressive or in any way required to play competitively.

cues.zh: 这些变现系统让你满意，并且真正提升你对这款投入几十小时游戏的享受……
cues.en: Monetization systems that leave you satisfied and actually increase your enjoyment of the game you're spending dozens of hours on...

cues.zh: 即使你选择只花很少的钱。
cues.en: Even if you choose to spend very little.

cues.zh: 但别搞错了：眼下我们真的只有这两个选择。
cues.en: But make no mistake: those really are our only two options right now.

cues.zh: 因为，就像我一开始说的：3A 游戏就不该再卖 60 美元了。
cues.en: Because, like I said at the beginning: AAA games just should not cost $60 anymore.

cues.zh: 下周见！
cues.en: See you next week!
